html:
The Upper Kuskokwim people, who call themselves Dichinanek' Hwt'ana, are an Athabaskan people of interior Alaska, living on the upper Kuskokwim River around today's McGrath and Nikolai, north-west of Denali.

They lived in small bands that moved with the seasons, hunting caribou and moose, trapping, and fishing salmon and whitefish. Downriver lived the Yup'ik, with whom they traded. Russian traders of Russian America reached the Kuskokwim in the 1830s and 1840s, and after the Alaska Purchase of 1867 American traders, missionaries and later gold seekers followed. Their language, Upper Kuskokwim, has only a few speakers today.
